summary: Iteration 9 — Admin 'Paiements SendavaPay' page validated end-to-end. Backend pytest 11/11 green: GET /api/admin/payments returns {items,count,counts:{total,pending,paid,failed,stuck}} with correct shape and no _id leak; status/stuck_only/q filters all behave as specified; POST /api/admin/payments/{ref}/reprocess returns 404 on unknown ref, {ok:true, already_activated:true} on already-activated payments, and on a synthetic stuck payment it sets activation_done=true and bumps user.max_level. Auth is enforced at the admin_router level (Depends(require_admin)) — unauth GET/POST both 401/403. Frontend: admin home shows the new '💳 Paiements SendavaPay' button (testID admin-open-payments-mgmt), clicking it navigates to /payments. The page renders the 5-cell stats grid (Total 8 / En attente 5 / Payés 3 / Échoués 0 / Bloqués 0), all five filter chips (filter-all/pending/paid/failed/stuck) toggle the list, payments-search filters in real-time (empty-state appears for non-matching query), open-pay-url-{ref} buttons render for the 5 pending rows, refresh and back work. With a synthetic stuck row injected in Mongo, force-activate-{ref} button appears under the 'Bloqués' filter as expected and successfully invokes POST /admin/payments/{ref}/reprocess. NOTE: when reprocess crashed (E11000 on matrix_placements because the test user already had a level-1 matrix row from a prior real activation), the UI correctly surfaced the backend error via window.alert — the button flow is wired correctly; the underlying activate_level non-idempotency is a separate hardening concern.

minor.issue: activate_level is not idempotent w.r.t. matrix_placements. If the previous (failed) activation already inserted the row in matrix_placements before the failure point, reprocess crashes with 500 'E11000 duplicate key error collection: spilivere.matrix_placements index: user_id_1_level_1'. The endpoint should either (a) treat E11000 on matrix_placements as a no-op and continue, or (b) check matrix_placements existence before insert. As-is, a real-world stuck payment whose failure happened *after* matrix placement cannot be unblocked from the new admin UI — the very use case the page was built for.

action_items: Make activate_level (or the matrix_placements insert inside it) idempotent: catch DuplicateKeyError on (user_id, level) and continue, or use update_one(..., upsert=True). Otherwise the 'Forcer l'activation' button fails on the most likely class of stuck payments — those where the matrix step succeeded but a later step failed.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line 1858-1902 (GET /admin/payments): clean, paginated, scrubs _id, aggregates counts in 5 separate count_documents calls — could be one aggregation pipeline if payments collection grows large, but fine for current scale.

server.py line 1905-1932 (POST .../reprocess): on activation failure it stores activation_error and re-raises 500, which is good for observability. But because activate_level is not idempotent for matrix_placements, the retry button currently 500s on any stuck payment whose matrix row already exists. This must be fixed before the admin tool is truly usable.
server.py is now 2345 lines — same recommendation as iter 7/8: extract admin/payments/settings into separate routers.

/app/frontend/app/(admin)/payments.tsx is well-scoped (255 lines), uses data-testid consistently, has loading/empty/error states. Good. Minor: window.confirm/window.alert are web-only — if the app is ever shipped to native, replace with Alert.alert from react-native.
seed_data_creation: Test fixtures auto-create/delete TEST_STUCK_* and TEST_OK_* payments and roll back max_level. The synthetic TEST_UI_STUCK_6cb44830 used for UI testing has been deleted. No production data touched.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The admin payments monitoring page is fully wired and functional. The only outstanding work is making activate_level idempotent so reprocess can recover payments whose matrix_placements row already exists. After that fix, re-run /app/backend/tests/test_admin_payments_mgmt.py (it covers the happy path) and additionally insert a payments doc with a user that already has a matrix_placements row at that level to verify reprocess no longer 500s.
rca_of_the_issue: Reproduction of the activate_level idempotency bug: 1) insert in db.payments a stuck row {status:'paid', activation_done:false, user_id:<existing user with level 1 placement>, level:1}. 2) POST /api/admin/payments/{ref}/reprocess. 3) Observe 500 with 'E11000 duplicate key error collection: spilivere.matrix_placements index: user_id_1_level_1'. Mitigation: in activate_level, wrap the matrix_placements insert in try/except DuplicateKeyError and treat duplicate as already-placed; alternatively use db.matrix_placements.update_one(filter, {'$setOnInsert': doc}, upsert=True). Then the rest of activate_level (max_level bump, commissions, etc.) can finish and activation_done=true gets set.
